ta%20filtering%20and%20to%20the%20most%20basic%20filters%20used%20to%20process%20biomechanical%20data%3A%20the%20moving%20average%2C%20the%20Butterworth%20filter%2C%20the%20critically%20damped%20filter%20and%20a%20few%20others.%20It%20starts%20from%20a%20concrete%20problem%2C%20getting%20an%20acceleration%20out%20of%20measured%20positions%2C%20and%20keeps%20coming%20back%20to%20it%20until%20the%20problem%20is%20solved%20reasonably%20well.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20You%20should%20be%20familiar%20with%20the%20%5Bbasic%20properties%20of%20signals%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fsignal_basic_properties.py)%20before%20proceeding%3A%20frequency%2C%20harmonics%2C%20sampling%2C%20noise%20and%20the%20signal-to-noise%20ratio.%20Finite%20differences%2C%20as%20used%20in%20%5BKinematics%20of%20a%20particle%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fkinematics_particle.py)%2C%20will%20also%20come%20up.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Read%20it%20in%20order%20and%20run%20each%20cell%20as%20you%20reach%20it.%20Work%20through%20the%20distributed%20Exercises%20before%20opening%20their%20solutions.%20The%20final%20Problems%20have%20collapsed%20final%20answers%20for%20independent%20practice.%20Where%20you%20find%20a%20**Challenge**%20or%20a%20set%20of%20**Guiding%20questions**%2C%20stop%20and%20answer%20on%20a%20scratchpad%20before%20moving%20on.%20Several%20of%20them%20ask%20you%20to%20predict%20a%20number%20*before*%20the%20code%20prints%20it%3B%20the%20prediction%20is%20the%20point%2C%20and%20being%20wrong%20is%20the%20most%20useful%20thing%20that%20can%20happen%20to%20you%20here.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Think%20of%20a%20quantity%20you%20would%20like%20to%20know%20but%20can%20only%20get%20by%20differentiating%20a%20measured%20position%3A%20the%20acceleration%20of%20a%20body%20segment%2C%20the%20velocity%20of%20a%20marker%2C%20the%20jerk%20of%20a%20reaching%20movement.%20If%20the%20position%20has%20an%20error%20of%201%20mm%2C%20guess%20how%20large%20the%20error%20in%20the%20acceleration%20will%20be.%20Write%20the%20guess%20down%3B%20you%20will%20be%20able%20to%20check%20its%20order%20of%20magnitude%20on%20real%20data%20in%20a%20moment.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20%20NumPy%20and%20SciPy%20do%20the%20computation%20(SciPy's%20%60signal%60%20module%20has%20the%20filters)%2C%20pandas%20reads%20the%20data%20files%2C%20and%20Matplotlib%20draws%20the%20plots.%20These%20packages%20are%20declared%20in%20the%20notebook%20metadata.%20Open%20the%20file%20in%20marimo%3B%20the%20Pezzack%2C%20EMG%20and%20ball-toss%20examples%20need%20access%20to%20the%20repository%20data.%20No%20motion-capture%20hardware%20or%20video%20software%20is%20needed%20to%20run%20the%20supplied%20examples.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20timeit%0A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%20%20%20%20import%20pandas%20as%20pd%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib.pyplot%20as%20plt%0A%20%20%20%20from%20scipy%20import%20interpolate%2C%20signal%0A%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22axes%22%2C%20labelsize%3D13%2C%20titlesize%3D14)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22xtick%22%2C%20labelsize%3D11)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22ytick%22%2C%20labelsize%3D11)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22legend%22%2C%20fontsize%3D11)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20interpolate%2C%20np%2C%20pd%2C%20plt%2C%20signal%2C%20timeit%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20The%20problem%3A%20an%20acceleration%20from%20measured%20positions%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%201977%2C%20Pezzack%2C%20Norman%20and%20Winter%20published%20a%20paper%20investigating%20the%20effects%20of%20differentiation%20and%20filtering%20on%20experimental%20data.%20They%20filmed%20a%20bar%20being%20rotated%20by%20hand%20in%20a%20horizontal%20plane%2C%20digitized%20its%20angle%20from%20the%20film%2C%20and%20at%20the%20same%20time%20measured%20its%20angular%20acceleration%20directly%2C%20with%20an%20accelerometer.%20Since%20then%20these%20data%20have%20become%20a%20benchmark%20for%20testing%20new%20algorithms%20(they%20are%20also%20available%20from%20the%20%5BISB%20website%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fisbweb.org%2Fdata%2Fpezzack%2Findex.html)).%20We%20will%20use%20the%20accelerometer's%20acceleration%20as%20an%20independent%20reference%2C%20recognizing%20that%20it%20too%20has%20measurement%20uncertainty%2C%20and%20ask%3A%20can%20we%20recover%20it%20from%20the%20angle%20alone%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20most%20direct%20answer%20is%20to%20differentiate%20the%20angle%20twice%20with%20finite%20differences.%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%20how%20the%20double-differentiated%20angle%20will%20compare%20with%20the%20measured%20acceleration.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20pd%2C%20plt)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_data%20%3D%20pd.read_csv(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20repo_file('data%2FPezzack.txt')%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20sep%3D%22%5Ct%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20header%3DNone%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20skiprows%3D6%2C%0A%20%20%20%20).to_numpy()%0A%20%20%20%20pz_time%2C%20pz_disp%2C%20pz_disp_noisy%2C%20pz_aacc%20%3D%20_data.T%0A%20%20%20%20pz_dt%20%3D%20np.mean(np.diff(pz_time))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20acceleration%20by%20the%20second-order%20finite%20difference%20(2%20samples%20shorter)%0A%20%20%20%20pz_aacc_diff%20%3D%20np.diff(pz_disp%2C%202)%20%2F%20pz_dt**2%0A%20%20%20%20_rmse%20%3D%20np.sqrt(np.mean((pz_aacc_diff%20-%20pz_aacc%5B1%3A-1%5D)%20**%202))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_fig%2C%20_axs%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%202%2C%20figsize%3D(11%2C%204))%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%5D.plot(pz_time%2C%20pz_disp%2C%20%22b.-%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%5D.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%5D.set_ylabel(%22Angular%20displacement%20%5Brad%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%5D.plot(pz_time%2C%20pz_aacc%2C%20%22g%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22Accelerometer%20(reference)%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%5D.plot(pz_time%5B1%3A-1%5D%2C%20pz_aacc_diff%2C%20%22r%22%2C%20label%3D%22Angle%20differentiated%20twice%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%5D.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%5D.set_ylabel(%22Angular%20acceleration%20%5Brad%2Fs%24%5E2%24%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%5D.legend(frameon%3DFalse%2C%20loc%3D%22upper%20left%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.suptitle(%22Pezzack's%20benchmark%20data%22%2C%20fontsize%3D16)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22Sampling%20interval%3A%20%7Bpz_dt%3A.4f%7D%20s%20(%7B1%20%2F%20pz_dt%3A.1f%7D%20Hz)%2C%20%7Bpz_time.size%7D%20samples%22)%0A%20%20%20%20print(f%22RMSE%20of%20the%20differentiated%20acceleration%3A%20%7B_rmse%3A.1f%7D%20rad%2Fs2%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20pz_aacc%2C%20pz_disp%2C%20pz_dt%2C%20pz_time%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20angle%20looks%20clean%3A%20a%20smooth%20curve%20with%20no%20visible%20noise.%20Its%20second%20derivative%20is%20not.%20The%20red%20curve%20follows%20the%20reference%20acceleration%20only%20roughly%2C%20with%20a%20jagged%20error%20of%20tens%20of%20rad%2Fs%C2%B2%20in%20places%20and%20an%20RMSE%20(root-mean-square%20error)%20of%20about%2011%20rad%2Fs%C2%B2.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20noise%20comes%20from%20small%20random%20errors%20in%20the%20digitization%20of%20each%20film%20frame%2C%20a%20fraction%20of%20a%20degree.%20Invisible%20in%20the%20angle%2C%20they%20dominate%20the%20acceleration.%20This%20notebook%20is%20about%20why%20that%20happens%20and%20what%20to%20do%20about%20it.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%200.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20errors%20in%20the%20angle%20are%20far%20too%20small%20to%20see%20in%20the%20left%20panel.%20Why%20do%20they%20become%20so%20large%20in%20the%20right%20one%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Is%20the%20error%20in%20the%20red%20curve%20larger%20where%20the%20acceleration%20is%20large%2C%20or%20is%20it%20spread%20over%20the%20whole%20recording%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Would%20sampling%20the%20film%20faster%2C%20with%20the%20same%20digitization%20error%20per%20frame%2C%20make%20the%20acceleration%20better%20or%20worse%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Why%20differentiation%20amplifies%20noise%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Removing%20noise%20from%20a%20signal%20is%20rarely%20trivial%2C%20and%20the%20problem%20gets%20worse%20with%20numerical%20differentiation%3A%20noise%20at%20frequencies%20higher%20than%20those%20of%20the%20signal%20is%20amplified%20by%20differentiation%2C%20so%20the%20signal-to-noise%20ratio%20(SNR)%20drops%20with%20each%20derivative.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20To%20see%20why%2C%20consider%20the%20following%20function%20representing%20some%20experimental%20data%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20f%20%3D%20%5Csin(%5Comega%20t)%20%2B%200.1%5Csin(10%5Comega%20t)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20first%20component%2C%20with%20a%20large%20amplitude%20(1)%20and%20a%20low%20frequency%20(1%20Hz)%2C%20represents%20the%20signal%3B%20the%20second%2C%20with%20a%20small%20amplitude%20(0.1)%20and%20a%20high%20frequency%20(10%20Hz)%2C%20represents%20the%20noise.%20The%20SNR%20of%20these%20data%20is%20%24(1%2F0.1)%5E2%20%3D%20100%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20you%20read%20on**%2C%20differentiate%20%24f%24%20twice%20by%20hand%20and%20predict%20the%20SNR%20of%20%24f'%24%20and%20of%20%24f''%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20f%5C%2C'%20%3D%20%5Comega%20%5Ccos(%5Comega%20t)%20%2B%20%5Comega%20%5Ccos(10%5Comega%20t)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20f%5C%2C''%20%3D%20-%5Comega%5E2%20%5Csin(%5Comega%20t)%20-%2010%5Comega%5E2%20%5Csin(10%5Comega%20t)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Each%20differentiation%20multiplies%20a%20component%20of%20frequency%20%24f%24%20by%20%242%5Cpi%20f%24%2C%20so%20the%2010%20Hz%20noise%20gains%20a%20factor%20of%2010%20on%20the%201%20Hz%20signal%20every%20time.%20For%20the%20first%20derivative%2C%20SNR%20%3D%201%2C%20and%20for%20the%20second%2C%20SNR%20%3D%200.01%3A%20the%20noise%20now%20has%20a%20hundred%20times%20the%20power%20of%20the%20signal.%20The%20following%20plots%20illustrate%20the%20problem%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20plt)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_t%20%3D%20np.arange(0%2C%201%2C%200.01)%0A%20%20%20%20_w%20%3D%202%20*%20np.pi%20*%201%20%20%23%201%20Hz%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20signal%20and%20noise%2C%20and%20their%20derivatives%0A%20%20%20%20_s%2C%20_n%20%3D%20np.sin(_w%20*%20_t)%2C%200.1%20*%20np.sin(10%20*%20_w%20*%20_t)%0A%20%20%20%20_sd%2C%20_nd%20%3D%20_w%20*%20np.cos(_w%20*%20_t)%2C%20_w%20*%20np.cos(10%20*%20_w%20*%20_t)%0A%20%20%20%20_sdd%2C%20_ndd%20%3D%20-_w%20*%20_w%20*%20np.sin(_w%20*%20_t)%2C%20-_w%20*%20_w%20*%2010%20*%20np.sin(10%20*%20_w%20*%20_t)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_fig%2C%20_axs%20%3D%20plt.subplots(3%2C%201%2C%20sharex%3DTrue%2C%20figsize%3D(9%2C%206.5))%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%5D.set_title(%22Differentiation%20of%20signal%20and%20noise%22)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_ax%2C%20_sig%2C%20_noi%2C%20_label%20in%20zip(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_axs%2C%20(_s%2C%20_sd%2C%20_sdd)%2C%20(_n%2C%20_nd%2C%20_ndd)%2C%20(%22f%22%2C%20%22f%20'%22%2C%20%22f%20''%22)%0A%20%20%20%20)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_t%2C%20_sig%2C%20%22b.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D1%2C%20label%3D%22signal%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_t%2C%20_noi%2C%20%22g.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D1%2C%20label%3D%22noise%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_t%2C%20_sig%20%2B%20_noi%2C%20%22r.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22signal%2Bnoise%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_ax.set_ylabel(_label)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%5D.legend(frameon%3DFalse%2C%20fontsize%3D10%2C%20loc%3D%22upper%20right%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B2%5D.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%20top%20panel%20the%20noise%20is%20a%20small%20ripple%20on%20the%20signal.%20In%20the%20bottom%20panel%20the%20signal%20is%20the%20small%20one.%20That%20is%20the%20Pezzack%20acceleration%20in%20miniature%2C%20and%20it%20points%20to%20the%20remedy%3A%20if%20the%20noise%20lives%20at%20higher%20frequencies%20than%20the%20signal%2C%20remove%20those%20frequencies%20*before*%20differentiating.%20That%20is%20what%20a%20low-pass%20filter%20does.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Filter%20and%20smoothing%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20data%20acquisition%20with%20an%20instrument%2C%20the%20noise%20often%20has%20higher%20frequencies%20and%20lower%20amplitudes%20than%20the%20signal%20of%20interest.%20Removing%20it%20is%20called%20filtering%20or%20smoothing.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FFilter_(signal_processing)%22%3EFiltering%3C%2Fa%3E%20is%20a%20process%20that%20attenuates%20some%20unwanted%20component%20or%20feature%20of%20a%20signal.%20A%20filter%20usually%20removes%20certain%20frequency%20components%20of%20the%20data%2C%20according%20to%20its%20frequency%20response.%20The%20%5Bfrequency%20response%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FFrequency_response)%20is%20the%20quantitative%20measure%20of%20the%20output%20spectrum%20of%20a%20system%20in%20response%20to%20a%20stimulus%2C%20and%20is%20used%20to%20characterize%20the%20dynamics%20of%20the%20system.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%5BSmoothing%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FSmoothing)%20is%20the%20removal%20of%20local%20(short-scale)%20fluctuations%20from%20the%20data%20while%20preserving%20a%20more%20global%20pattern%20(those%20local%20variations%20could%20be%20noise%2C%20or%20just%20a%20short-scale%20phenomenon%20that%20is%20not%20of%20interest).%20A%20filter%20with%20a%20low-pass%20frequency%20response%20performs%20smoothing.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20With%20respect%20to%20its%20implementation%2C%20a%20filter%20can%20be%20an%20%5Banalog%20filter%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FPassive_analogue_filter_development)%20or%20a%20%5Bdigital%20filter%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FDigital_filter).%20An%20analog%20filter%20is%20an%20electronic%20circuit%20that%20filters%20an%20input%20electrical%20signal%20and%20outputs%20a%20filtered%20electrical%20signal%3B%20a%20simple%20one%20can%20be%20built%20with%20a%20resistor%20and%20a%20capacitor.%20A%20digital%20filter%20is%20a%20system%20that%20filters%20digital%20(discrete-time)%20data.%20The%20anti-aliasing%20filter%20of%20an%20acquisition%20system%20must%20be%20analog%2C%20because%20it%20acts%20before%20sampling%3B%20everything%20in%20this%20notebook%20is%20digital%2C%20and%20acts%20on%20data%20already%20recorded.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Example%3A%20the%20moving-average%20filter%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20simple%20low-pass%20(smoothing)%20filter%20is%20the%20moving%20average%3A%20the%20arithmetic%20mean%20of%20successive%20subsequences%20of%20%24m%24%20terms%20of%20the%20data.%20For%20instance%2C%20the%20moving%20averages%20with%20window%20sizes%20%24m%24%20equal%20to%202%20and%203%20are%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%7D%0A%20%20%20%20y_%7BMA(2)%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%5Bx_1%2Bx_2%2C%5C%3B%20x_2%2Bx_3%2C%5C%3B%20%5Ccdots%2C%5C%3B%20x_%7Bn-1%7D%2Bx_n%5D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20y_%7BMA(3)%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B3%7D%5Bx_1%2Bx_2%2Bx_3%2C%5C%3B%20x_2%2Bx_3%2Bx_4%2C%5C%3B%20%5Ccdots%2C%5C%3B%20x_%7Bn-2%7D%2Bx_%7Bn-1%7D%2Bx_n%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20with%20the%20general%20formula%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20y%5Bi%5D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bm%7D%5Csum_%7Bj%3D0%7D%5E%7Bm-1%7D%20x%5Bi%2Bj%5D%20%5Cquad%20%5Ctext%7Bfor%7D%20%5Cquad%20i%3D1%2C%20%5C%3B%20%5Cdots%2C%20%5C%3B%20n-m%2B1%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24n%24%20is%20the%20number%20of%20data.%20Here%20is%20a%20naive%20implementation%2C%20with%20a%20loop%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20moving_average(x%2C%20window)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Moving%20average%20of%20%60x%60%20with%20window%20size%20%60window%60%20(a%20naive%20loop).%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20y%20%3D%20np.empty(len(x)%20-%20window%20%2B%201)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20i%20in%20range(len(y))%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20y%5Bi%5D%20%3D%20np.sum(x%5Bi%20%3A%20i%20%2B%20window%5D)%20%2F%20window%0A%20%20%20%20return%20y%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20test%20it%20on%20a%20signal%20that%20jumps%20from%200%20to%201%20and%20back%2C%20plus%20random%20noise%20with%20a%20standard%20deviation%20of%200.1.%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%20what%20a%20window%20of%2011%20samples%20will%20do%20to%20the%20noise%2C%20and%20what%20it%20will%20do%20to%20the%20two%20jumps.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20plt)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_rng%20%3D%20np.random.default_rng(seed%3D42)%0A%20%20%20%20_signal%20%3D%20np.zeros(300)%0A%20%20%20%20_signal%5B100%3A200%5D%20%2B%3D%201%0A%20%20%20%20_x%20%3D%20_signal%20%2B%20_rng.standard_normal(300)%20%2F%2010%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_y%20%3D%20moving_average(_x%2C%2011)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_ax%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%201%2C%20figsize%3D(9%2C%204))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_x%2C%20%22b.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D1%2C%20label%3D%22raw%20data%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_y%2C%20%22r.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22moving%20average%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.legend(frameon%3DFalse%2C%20loc%3D%22upper%20right%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_xlabel(%22Sample%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_ylabel(%22Amplitude%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22Standard%20deviation%20of%20the%20noise%2C%20before%3A%20%7Bnp.std(_x%5B%3A90%5D)%3A.3f%7D%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22after%3A%20%7Bnp.std(_y%5B%3A85%5D)%3A.3f%7D%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20noise%20is%20reduced%20several%20times.%20Averaging%20%24m%24%20independent%20values%20reduces%20their%20standard%20deviation%20by%20%24%5Csqrt%7Bm%7D%24%20on%20average%2C%20about%203.3%20for%20%24m%20%3D%2011%24%3B%20an%20estimate%20from%20a%20stretch%20of%20data%20this%20short%20scatters%20a%20good%20deal%20around%20that%20value.%20The%20price%20is%20paid%20at%20the%20jumps%3A%20each%20one%20is%20now%20a%20ramp%2011%20samples%20long.%20Every%20low-pass%20filter%20makes%20this%20trade%20between%20noise%20and%20sharpness%3B%20the%20rest%20of%20the%20notebook%20is%20about%20making%20it%20well.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Look%20also%20at%20*where*%20the%20jumps%20are.%20The%20raw%20data%20jump%20at%20samples%20100%20and%20200%2C%20the%20filtered%20ones%20about%205%20samples%20earlier.%20The%20output%20%60y%5Bi%5D%60%20is%20the%20mean%20of%20%60x%5Bi%5D%60%20to%20%60x%5Bi%2B10%5D%60%2C%20centred%20on%20sample%20%60i%2B5%60%2C%20but%20we%20plotted%20it%20at%20%60i%60.%20We%20will%20come%20back%20to%20this%2C%20and%20to%20faster%20implementations%20of%20the%20moving%20average%2C%20later.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%202.**%20Apply%20a%20three-point%20moving%20average%20to%20%24%5B0%2C0%2C3%2C0%2C0%5D%24.%20What%20happens%20to%20a%20constant%20sequence%20of%203%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%202%0A%20%20%20%20The%20valid%20windows%20have%20sums%203%2C%203%20and%203%2C%20giving%20%24%5B1%2C1%2C1%5D%24.%20A%20constant%20sequence%20has%20window%20sums%209%2C%20giving%203%20at%20every%20complete%20window%3A%20the%20coefficients%20sum%20to%20one.%20The%20isolated%20peak%20is%20spread%20in%20time%2C%20explaining%20both%20the%20smoothing%20and%20the%20loss%20of%20sharpness.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Digital%20filters%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20signal%20processing%2C%20a%20digital%20filter%20is%20a%20system%20that%20performs%20mathematical%20operations%20on%20a%20signal%20to%20modify%20certain%20aspects%20of%20it.%20A%20digital%20filter%20(more%20precisely%2C%20a%20causal%2C%20linear%2C%20time-invariant%20(LTI)%20digital%20filter)%20can%20be%20seen%20as%20the%20implementation%20of%20the%20following%20difference%20equation%20in%20the%20time%20domain%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20y_n%20%26%3D%20b_0x_n%20%2B%20b_1x_%7Bn-1%7D%20%2B%20%5Ccdots%20%2B%20b_Mx_%7Bn-M%7D%20-%20a_1y_%7Bn-1%7D%20-%20%5Ccdots%20-%20a_Ny_%7Bn-N%7D%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%26%3D%20%5Csum_%7Bk%3D0%7D%5EM%20b_kx_%7Bn-k%7D%20-%20%5Csum_%7Bk%3D1%7D%5EN%20a_ky_%7Bn-k%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20the%20output%20%24y%24%20is%20the%20filtered%20version%20of%20the%20input%20%24x%24%2C%20%24a_k%24%20and%20%24b_k%24%20are%20the%20filter%20coefficients%20(real%20values)%2C%20and%20the%20order%20of%20the%20filter%20is%20the%20larger%20of%20%24N%24%20and%20%24M%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20This%20general%20equation%20describes%20a%20recursive%20filter%3A%20the%20filtered%20value%20%24y_n%24%20is%20computed%20from%20current%20and%20previous%20values%20of%20%24x%24%20*and*%20from%20previous%20values%20of%20%24y%24%2C%20its%20own%20output%3B%20it%20is%20a%20system%20with%20feedback.%20A%20filter%20that%20does%20not%20reuse%20its%20outputs%20as%20inputs%20(a%20system%20with%20only%20feedforward)%20is%20called%20nonrecursive%2C%20and%20its%20%24a%24%20coefficients%20are%20zero.%20Recursive%20and%20nonrecursive%20filters%20are%20also%20known%20as%20infinite%20impulse%20response%20(IIR)%20and%20finite%20impulse%20response%20(FIR)%20filters%2C%20respectively.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20filter%20with%20only%20the%20terms%20on%20previous%20values%20of%20%24y%24%20is%20also%20known%20as%20an%20autoregressive%20(AR)%20filter%3B%20one%20with%20only%20the%20terms%20on%20current%20and%20previous%20values%20of%20%24x%24%2C%20as%20a%20moving-average%20(MA)%20filter%3B%20and%20one%20with%20both%2C%20as%20an%20autoregressive%20moving-average%20(ARMA)%20filter.%20The%20moving%20average%20of%20the%20previous%20section%20is%20an%20FIR%20filter%20with%20%24m%24%20coefficients%20%24b%24%2C%20each%20equal%20to%20%241%2Fm%24%2C%20and%20all%20%24a%24%20coefficients%20equal%20to%20zero.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Transfer%20function%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Another%20way%20to%20characterize%20a%20filter%20is%20by%20its%20%5Btransfer%20function%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FTransfer_function).%20In%20simple%20terms%2C%20the%20transfer%20function%20is%20the%20ratio%2C%20in%20the%20frequency%20domain%2C%20between%20the%20output%20and%20the%20input%20signals%20of%20a%20filter.%20For%20a%20continuous-time%20input%20%24x(t)%24%20and%20output%20%24y(t)%24%2C%20the%20transfer%20function%20%24H(s)%24%20is%20the%20ratio%20between%20the%20%5BLaplace%20transforms%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FLaplace_transform)%20of%20the%20output%20and%20of%20the%20input%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20H(s)%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7BY(s)%7D%7BX(s)%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24s%20%3D%20%5Csigma%20%2B%20j%5Comega%24%2C%20%24j%24%20is%20the%20imaginary%20unit%20and%20%24%5Comega%24%20is%20the%20angular%20frequency%2C%20%242%5Cpi%20f%24.%20In%20the%20steady-state%20response%20we%20can%20take%20%24%5Csigma%3D0%24%2C%20and%20the%20Laplace%20transforms%20with%20complex%20argument%20reduce%20to%20%5BFourier%20transforms%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FFourier_transform)%20with%20real%20argument%20%24%5Comega%24.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20a%20discrete-time%20input%20and%20output%2C%20the%20transfer%20function%20%24H(z)%24%20is%20the%20ratio%20between%20their%20%5Bz-transforms%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FZ-transform)%2C%20and%20the%20formalism%20is%20similar.%20Taking%20the%20z-transform%20of%20the%20difference%20equation%20above%20gives%20the%20transfer%20function%20of%20a%20linear%2C%20time-invariant%2C%20causal%20digital%20filter%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20H(z)%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7BY(z)%7D%7BX(z)%7D%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7Bb_0%20%2B%20b_1%20z%5E%7B-1%7D%20%2B%20b_2%20z%5E%7B-2%7D%20%2B%20%5Ccdots%20%2B%20b_M%20z%5E%7B-M%7D%7D%7B1%20%2B%20a_1%20z%5E%7B-1%7D%20%2B%20a_2%20z%5E%7B-2%7D%20%2B%20%5Ccdots%20%2B%20a_N%20z%5E%7B-N%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%3D%20%5Cfrac%7B%5Csum_%7Bk%3D0%7D%5EM%20b_kz%5E%7B-k%7D%7D%7B1%20%2B%20%5Csum_%7Bk%3D1%7D%5EN%20a_kz%5E%7B-k%7D%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20and%20again%20the%20order%20of%20the%20filter%20is%20the%20larger%20of%20%24N%24%20and%20%24M%24.%20As%20with%20the%20difference%20equation%2C%20this%20is%20the%20transfer%20function%20of%20a%20recursive%20(IIR)%20filter%3B%20if%20the%20%24a%24%20coefficients%20are%20zero%2C%20the%20denominator%20equals%20one%20and%20the%20filter%20is%20nonrecursive%20(FIR).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20The%20Fourier%20transform%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20%5BFourier%20transform%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FFourier_transform)%20is%20a%20mathematical%20operation%20that%20transforms%20a%20signal%20that%20is%20a%20function%20of%20time%2C%20%24g(t)%24%2C%20into%20a%20function%20of%20frequency%2C%20%24G(f)%24%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathcal%7BF%7D%5Bg(t)%5D%20%3D%20G(f)%20%3D%20%5Cint_%7B-%5Cinfty%7D%5E%7B%5Cinfty%7D%20g(t)%5C%2C%20e%5E%7B-j%202%5Cpi%20f%20t%7D%5C%2C%20dt%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Its%20inverse%20operation%20is%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cmathcal%7BF%7D%5E%7B-1%7D%5BG(f)%5D%20%3D%20g(t)%20%3D%20%5Cint_%7B-%5Cinfty%7D%5E%7B%5Cinfty%7D%20G(f)%5C%2C%20e%5E%7Bj%202%5Cpi%20f%20t%7D%5C%2C%20df%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24G(f)%24%20is%20the%20representation%20of%20the%20time-domain%20signal%20%24g(t)%24%20in%20the%20frequency%20domain%2C%20and%20vice%20versa%3B%20the%20two%20are%20called%20a%20Fourier%20transform%20pair.%20See%20the%20notebook%20%5BFourier%20transform%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Ffourier_transform.py)%2C%20or%20%5Bthis%20text%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thefouriertransform.com%2Ftransform%2Ffourier.php)%2C%20for%20an%20introduction.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Types%20of%20filters%0A%0A%20%20%20%20With%20respect%20to%20the%20frequencies%20that%20are%20*not*%20removed%20from%20the%20data%2C%20with%20a%20boundary%20given%20by%20the%20critical%20or%20cutoff%20frequency%2C%20a%20filter%20can%20be%20low-pass%2C%20high-pass%2C%20band-pass%20or%20band-stop.%20The%20frequency%20responses%20of%20these%20filters%20are%20illustrated%20in%20the%20next%20figure.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cfigure%20aria-describedby%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%3E%3Ccenter%3E%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fthumb.wikimedia.org%2Fwikipedia%2Fcommons%2Fthumb%2Fe%2Fec%2FBandform_template.svg%2F960px-Bandform_template.svg.png%22%20width%3D500%20alt%3D%22Filters%22%2F%3E%3C%2Fcenter%3E%3C%2Ffigure%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cspan%20id%3D%22figure-caption-1%22%20class%3D%22figure-caption%22%20style%3D%22display%3Ablock%3Btext-align%3Acenter%3Bfont-style%3Aitalic%22%3EFigure.%20Frequency%20response%20of%20filters%20(%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FFilter_(signal_processing)%22%3Efrom%20Wikipedia%3C%2Fa%3E).%3C%2Fspan%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20critical%20or%20cutoff%20frequency%20of%20a%20filter%20is%20the%20frequency%20at%20which%20the%20power%20(the%20amplitude%20squared)%20of%20the%20filtered%20signal%20is%20half%20the%20power%20of%20the%20input%20signal%2C%20or%2C%20equivalently%2C%20the%20output%20amplitude%20is%200.707%20times%20the%20input%20amplitude.%20For%20instance%2C%20if%20a%20low-pass%20filter%20has%20a%20cutoff%20frequency%20of%2010%20Hz%2C%20a%2010%20Hz%20component%20comes%20out%20with%2050%25%20of%20its%20power%20and%20about%2071%25%20of%20its%20amplitude.%20(The%20same%20%241%2F%5Csqrt%7B2%7D%24%20as%20the%20RMS%20of%20a%20sinusoid%2C%20in%20%5BBasic%20properties%20of%20signals%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fsignal_basic_properties.py).)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20gain%20of%20a%20filter%20(the%20ratio%20between%20the%20output%20and%20input%20powers)%20is%20usually%20expressed%20in%20decibels%20(dB).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Decibel%20(dB)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FDecibel%22%3Edecibel%20(dB)%3C%2Fa%3E%20is%20a%20logarithmic%20unit%20used%20to%20express%20the%20ratio%20between%20two%20values.%20For%20the%20gain%20of%20a%20filter%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20Gain%3D10%5C%2C%5Clog_%7B10%7D%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7BA_%7Bout%7D%5E2%7D%7BA_%7Bin%7D%5E2%7D%5Cright)%3D20%5C%2C%5Clog_%7B10%7D%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7BA_%7Bout%7D%7D%7BA_%7Bin%7D%7D%5Cright)%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24A_%7Bout%7D%24%20and%20%24A_%7Bin%7D%24%20are%20the%20amplitudes%20of%20the%20output%20(filtered)%20and%20input%20(raw)%20signals.%20A%20decibel%20is%20one%20tenth%20of%20a%20bel%2C%20a%20unit%20named%20in%20honor%20of%20%3Ca%20href%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FAlexander_Graham_Bell%22%3EAlexander%20Graham%20Bell%3C%2Fa%3E.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%20the%20gain%20in%20decibels%20at%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%2C%20where%20the%20power%20is%20halved%2C%20and%20for%20an%20output%20amplitude%20attenuated%20by%20a%20factor%20of%2010%20and%20of%201000.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Amplitude%20ratio%20%20%20Power%20ratio%20%20%20Gain%20%5BdB%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_ratio%20in%20(10%2C%202%2C%201%2C%201%20%2F%20np.sqrt(2)%2C%200.5%2C%200.1%2C%200.001)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(f%22%7B_ratio%3A15.4f%7D%20%7B_ratio**2%3A13.6f%7D%20%7B20%20*%20np.log10(_ratio)%3A11.1f%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20cutoff%20frequency%20is%20the%20**%24-3%24%20dB**%20point%3A%20%2410%5Clog_%7B10%7D(0.5)%20%5Capprox%20-3%24%20dB.%20Doubling%20the%20power%20is%20%24%2B3%24%20dB.%20Every%20factor%20of%20ten%20in%20amplitude%20is%2020%20dB%2C%20so%20an%20attenuation%20of%20the%20amplitude%20by%201000%20times%20is%20%24-60%24%20dB%2C%20and%20%24-120%24%20dB%20would%20be%20a%20million%20times.%20That%20compression%20is%20why%20the%20decibel%20is%20useful%20for%20describing%20filters%2C%20whose%20attenuation%20spans%20many%20orders%20of%20magnitude.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Butterworth%20filter%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20common%20filter%20in%20biomechanics%20and%20motor%20control%20is%20the%20%5BButterworth%20filter%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FButterworth_filter).%20It%20is%20popular%20because%20it%20is%20simple%20to%20design%20and%20to%20use%2C%20and%20because%20its%20frequency%20response%20is%20maximally%20flat%20in%20the%20pass%20band%3A%20it%20does%20not%20ripple%2C%20so%20the%20frequencies%20it%20keeps%20are%20kept%20with%20nearly%20the%20same%20gain.%20It%20is%20a%20recursive%20(IIR)%20filter%2C%20and%20both%20its%20%24a%24%20and%20%24b%24%20coefficients%20are%20used.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20SciPy%2C%20the%20function%20%60butter%60%20calculates%20the%20filter%20coefficients%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60python%0A%20%20%20%20butter(N%2C%20Wn%2C%20btype%3D'low'%2C%20analog%3DFalse%2C%20output%3D'ba')%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%60N%60%20is%20the%20order%20of%20the%20filter%2C%20%60Wn%60%20is%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20given%20as%20a%20fraction%20of%20the%20%5BNyquist%20frequency%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FNyquist_frequency)%20(half%20the%20sampling%20frequency)%2C%20and%20%60btype%60%20is%20the%20type%20of%20filter%20(one%20of%20%60'lowpass'%60%2C%20%60'highpass'%60%2C%20%60'bandpass'%60%2C%20%60'bandstop'%60%3B%20the%20default%20is%20%60'lowpass'%60).%20The%20filtering%20itself%20is%20done%20by%20the%20function%20%60lfilter%60%2C%20which%20implements%20the%20difference%20equation%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60python%0A%20%20%20%20lfilter(b%2C%20a%2C%20x%2C%20axis%3D-1%2C%20zi%3DNone)%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%60b%60%20and%20%60a%60%20are%20the%20coefficients%20calculated%20by%20%60butter%60%2C%20and%20%60x%60%20is%20the%20data%20to%20be%20filtered.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20filter%20the%20signal-plus-noise%20function%20from%20the%20section%20on%20differentiation%2C%20sampled%20at%20100%20Hz%2C%20with%20a%20second-order%20Butterworth%20low-pass%20filter%20at%205%20Hz%2C%20between%20the%201%20Hz%20signal%20and%20the%2010%20Hz%20noise.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20plt%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20fs%20%3D%20100%20%20%23%20sampling%20frequency%20%5BHz%5D%0A%20%20%20%20bw_t%20%3D%20np.arange(0%2C%201%2C%201%20%2F%20fs)%0A%20%20%20%20_w%20%3D%202%20*%20np.pi%20*%201%20%20%23%201%20Hz%0A%20%20%20%20bw_y%20%3D%20np.sin(_w%20*%20bw_t)%20%2B%200.1%20*%20np.sin(10%20*%20_w%20*%20bw_t)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20second-order%20Butterworth%20low-pass%20filter%20at%205%20Hz%0A%20%20%20%20_b%2C%20_a%20%3D%20signal.butter(2%2C%205%20%2F%20(fs%20%2F%202)%2C%20btype%3D%22low%22)%0A%20%20%20%20bw_y2%20%3D%20signal.lfilter(_b%2C%20_a%2C%20bw_y)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_ax%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%201%2C%20figsize%3D(9%2C%204))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(bw_t%2C%20bw_y%2C%20%22r.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22raw%20data%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(bw_t%2C%20bw_y2%2C%20%22b.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22filter%20%40%205%20Hz%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.legend(frameon%3DFalse)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_ylabel(%22Amplitude%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%20bw_t%2C%20bw_y%2C%20bw_y2%2C%20fs%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20ripple%20is%20gone.%20But%20the%20filtered%20signal%20is%20also%20late%3A%20the%20Butterworth%20filter%20introduces%20a%20phase%20shift%2C%20a%20delay%2C%20between%20the%20raw%20and%20filtered%20signals.%20We%20will%20measure%20it%2C%20and%20then%20remove%20it.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20First%2C%20a%20property%20of%20the%20coefficients.%20For%20a%20low-pass%20filter%20to%20leave%20a%20constant%20signal%20unchanged%20(a%20gain%20of%20one%20at%20zero%20frequency)%2C%20its%20transfer%20function%20at%20%24z%20%3D%201%24%20must%20equal%20one%2C%20and%20from%20the%20expression%20for%20%24H(z)%24%20this%20means%20that%20the%20sum%20of%20the%20%24b%24%20coefficients%20minus%20the%20sum%20of%20the%20%24a%24%20coefficients%2C%20excluding%20the%20first%2C%20is%20one%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Low-pass%20Butterworth%20filter%20coefficients%20(cutoff%20at%200.1%20of%20the%20Nyquist%20frequency)%22)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_order%20in%20(1%2C%202)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_b%2C%20_a%20%3D%20signal.butter(_order%2C%200.1%2C%20btype%3D%22low%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22Order%20%7B_order%7D%3A%5Cn%20%20b%3A%20%7B_b%7D%5Cn%20%20a%3A%20%7B_a%7D%5Cn%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%20%20sum(b)%20-%20sum(a%5B1%3A%5D)%20%3D%20%7Bnp.sum(_b)%20-%20np.sum(_a%5B1%3A%5D)%3A.6f%7D%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Bode%20plot%0A%0A%20%20%20%20How%20much%20the%20amplitude%20of%20the%20filtered%20signal%20is%20attenuated%20relative%20to%20the%20raw%20signal%2C%20as%20a%20function%20of%20frequency%2C%20is%20given%20by%20the%20frequency%20response.%20The%20plots%20of%20the%20magnitude%20and%20phase%20responses%20form%20the%20%5BBode%20plot%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FBode_plot).%20Here%20it%20is%20for%20the%20filter%20we%20just%20used%20(Butterworth%2C%20low-pass%20at%205%20Hz%2C%20second%20order)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(fs%2C%20np%2C%20plt%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_b%2C%20_a%20%3D%20signal.butter(2%2C%205%20%2F%20(fs%20%2F%202)%2C%20btype%3D%22low%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_f%2C%20_h%20%3D%20signal.freqz(_b%2C%20_a%2C%20worN%3D512%2C%20fs%3Dfs)%20%20%23%20frequency%20response%0A%20%20%20%20_angles%20%3D%20np.rad2deg(np.unwrap(np.angle(_h)))%20%20%23%20phase%20%5Bdegrees%5D%0A%20%20%20%20_h_db%20%3D%2020%20*%20np.log10(np.abs(_h))%20%20%23%20magnitude%20%5BdB%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_fig%2C%20(_ax1%2C%20_ax2)%20%3D%20plt.subplots(2%2C%201%2C%20sharex%3DTrue%2C%20figsize%3D(9%2C%206.5))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax1.plot(_f%2C%20_h_db%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax1.plot(5%2C%20-3.01%2C%20%22ro%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax1.set_ylim(-80%2C%203)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax1.set_title(%22Frequency%20response%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax1.set_ylabel(%22Magnitude%20%5BdB%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axi%20%3D%20_ax1.inset_axes(%5B0.06%2C%200.08%2C%200.33%2C%200.5%5D)%20%20%23%20zoom%20around%20the%20cutoff%0A%20%20%20%20_axi.plot(_f%2C%20_h_db%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_axi.plot(5%2C%20-3.01%2C%20%22ro%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axi.set_xlim(%5B0%2C%2010%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_axi.set_ylim(%5B-6%2C%200.5%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_axi.grid(True%2C%20linestyle%3D%22%3A%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax2.plot(_f%2C%20_angles%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax2.plot(5%2C%20-90%2C%20%22ro%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax2.set_title(%22Phase%20response%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax2.set_xlabel(%22Frequency%20%5BHz%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax2.set_ylabel(%22Phase%20%5Bdegrees%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20inset%20shows%20that%20at%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%2C%205%20Hz%2C%20the%20filtered%20signal%20is%20indeed%20attenuated%20by%203%20dB.%20The%20phase%20response%20shows%20that%20at%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%2C%20the%20output%20lags%20the%20input%20by%20%2490%5Eo%24.%20A%205%20Hz%20component%20has%20a%20period%20of%200.2%20s%2C%20so%20%2490%5Eo%24%2C%20a%20quarter%20of%20a%20period%2C%20is%20a%20delay%20of%200.05%20s.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20But%20the%20delay%20we%20saw%20in%20the%20plot%20was%20of%20the%201%20Hz%20signal%2C%20not%20of%20a%205%20Hz%20component.%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%20the%20delay%20of%20the%201%20Hz%20component.%20Is%20it%200.05%20s%2C%20five%20times%20longer%2C%20or%20something%20else%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(fs%2C%20np%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_b%2C%20_a%20%3D%20signal.butter(2%2C%205%20%2F%20(fs%20%2F%202)%2C%20btype%3D%22low%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_freqs%20%3D%20np.array(%5B1%2C%202%2C%205%2C%2010%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_h%20%3D%20signal.freqz(_b%2C%20_a%2C%20worN%3D_freqs%2C%20fs%3Dfs)%0A%20%20%20%20_phase%20%3D%20np.angle(_h)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%22Frequency%20%5BHz%5D%20%20%20Gain%20%5BdB%5D%20%20%20Phase%20%5Bdegrees%5D%20%20%20Delay%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20_f%2C%20_hh%2C%20_ph%20in%20zip(_freqs%2C%20_h%2C%20_phase)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%7B_f%3A14d%7D%20%7B20%20*%20np.log10(np.abs(_hh))%3A11.2f%7D%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22%7Bnp.rad2deg(_ph)%3A17.1f%7D%20%7B-_ph%20%2F%20(2%20*%20np.pi%20*%20_f)%3A11.3f%7D%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%201%20Hz%20component%20lags%20by%20only%20%2416%5Eo%24%2C%20but%20%2416%5Eo%24%20of%20a%201%20s%20period%20is%200.045%20s%2C%20almost%20the%20same%20delay%20as%20the%205%20Hz%20component.%20In%20its%20pass%20band%2C%20the%20phase%20of%20the%20Butterworth%20filter%20grows%20nearly%20in%20proportion%20to%20the%20frequency%2C%20so%20every%20component%20the%20filter%20keeps%20is%20delayed%20by%20roughly%20the%20same%20time%2C%20about%20%24%5Csqrt%7B2%7D%2F(2%5Cpi%20f_c)%20%5Capprox%200.045%24%20s%20for%20this%20second-order%20filter.%20The%20filtered%20signal%20is%20close%20to%20a%20delayed%20copy%20of%20the%20slow%20part%20of%20the%20raw%20one.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20delay%20of%2045%20ms%20is%20not%20a%20detail.%20If%20you%20filter%20a%20kinematic%20signal%20this%20way%20and%20compare%20it%20with%20an%20EMG%20or%20a%20force%20filtered%20differently%2C%20every%20timing%20between%20them%20is%20off%20by%20that%20much.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Order%20of%20a%20filter%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20order%20of%20a%20filter%20determines%20how%20steep%20the%20%22wall%22%20of%20the%20frequency%20response%20is%20around%20the%20cutoff%20frequency.%20A%20vertical%20wall%20exactly%20at%20the%20cutoff%20would%20be%20ideal%2C%20but%20it%20is%20impossible%20to%20implement.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20first-order%20Butterworth%20filter%20attenuates%206%20dB%20for%20each%20doubling%20of%20the%20frequency%20(per%20octave)%2C%20or%2C%20which%20is%20the%20same%2C%2020%20dB%20each%20time%20the%20frequency%20is%20multiplied%20by%2010%20(per%20decade).%20In%20technical%20terms%2C%20a%20first-order%20filter%20rolls%20off%20at%20%24-6%24%20dB%20per%20octave%2C%20or%20%24-20%24%20dB%20per%20decade.%20A%20second-order%20filter%20rolls%20off%20at%20%24-12%24%20dB%20per%20octave%20(%24-40%24%20dB%20per%20decade)%2C%20and%20so%20on%2C%20as%20the%20next%20figure%20shows.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20butterworth_plot()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Plot%20the%20frequency%20response%20of%20Butterworth%20filters%20of%20different%20orders.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib.pyplot%20as%20plt%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%20%20%20%20from%20scipy%20import%20signal%0A%0A%20%20%20%20fig%2C%20ax%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%202%2C%20figsize%3D(11%2C%204.2))%0A%20%20%20%20colors%20%3D%20%7B1%3A%20%22b%22%2C%202%3A%20%22r%22%2C%204%3A%20%22g%22%2C%206%3A%20%22y%22%7D%0A%20%20%20%20for%20order%2C%20color%20in%20colors.items()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b%2C%20a%20%3D%20signal.butter(order%2C%2010%2C%20%22low%22%2C%20analog%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20w%2C%20h%20%3D%20signal.freqs(b%2C%20a%2C%20worN%3Dnp.logspace(0%2C%202%2C%20500))%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ax%5B0%5D.plot(w%20%2F%2010%2C%2020%20*%20np.log10(abs(h))%2C%20color%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20ax%5B1%5D.plot(w%20%2F%2010%2C%20np.rad2deg(np.unwrap(np.angle(h)))%2C%20color%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20for%20axi%20in%20ax%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20axi.axvline(1%2C%20color%3D%22black%22)%20%20%23%20cutoff%20frequency%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20axi.set_xscale(%22log%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20axi.set_xlabel(%22Frequency%20%2F%20Critical%20frequency%22)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20axi.grid(which%3D%22both%22%2C%20axis%3D%22both%22)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B0%5D.scatter(1%2C%20-3%2C%20marker%3D%22s%22%2C%20edgecolor%3D%220%22%2C%20facecolor%3D%221%22%2C%20s%3D400)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B0%5D.set_ylabel(%22Magnitude%20%5BdB%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B0%5D.set_xlim(0.1%2C%2010)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B0%5D.set_ylim(-120%2C%2010)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B1%5D.legend(%5Bstr(order)%20for%20order%20in%20colors%5D%2C%20title%3D%22Filter%20order%22%2C%20loc%3D%22best%22)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B1%5D.set_ylabel(%22Phase%20%5Bdegrees%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B1%5D.set_yticks(np.arange(0%2C%20-300%2C%20-45))%0A%20%20%20%20ax%5B1%5D.set_ylim(-300%2C%2010)%0A%20%20%20%20axi%20%3D%20ax%5B0%5D.inset_axes(%5B0.08%2C%200.08%2C%200.38%2C%200.45%5D)%20%20%23%20zoom%20around%20the%20cutoff%0A%20%20%20%20for%20order%2C%20color%20in%20colors.items()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b%2C%20a%20%3D%20signal.butter(order%2C%2010%2C%20%22low%22%2C%20analog%3DTrue)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20w%2C%20h%20%3D%20signal.freqs(b%2C%20a%2C%20worN%3Dnp.linspace(5%2C%2015%2C%20200))%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20axi.plot(w%20%2F%2010%2C%2020%20*%20np.log10(abs(h))%2C%20color%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20axi.set_xticks((0.6%2C%201%2C%201.4))%0A%20%20%20%20axi.set_yticks((-6%2C%20-3%2C%200))%0A%20%20%20%20axi.set_ylim(%5B-7%2C%201%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20axi.set_xlim(%5B0.5%2C%201.5%5D)%0A%20%20%20%20axi.grid(which%3D%22both%22%2C%20axis%3D%22both%22)%0A%20%20%20%20fig.suptitle(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22Bode%20plot%20of%20low-pass%20Butterworth%20filters%20of%20different%20orders%22%2C%20fontsize%3D15%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20butterworth_plot()%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20All%20orders%20pass%20through%20%24-3%24%20dB%20at%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20(the%20square).%20Above%20it%2C%20the%20higher%20orders%20fall%20much%20faster%3A%20at%20ten%20times%20the%20cutoff%20a%20first-order%20filter%20has%20attenuated%20by%2020%20dB%2C%20a%20sixth-order%20one%20by%20120%20dB.%20Note%20the%20cost%20in%20the%20right%20panel%2C%20though%3A%20the%20higher%20the%20order%2C%20the%20larger%20the%20phase%20lag.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%201.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Read%20the%20left%20panel%20at%20twice%20the%20cutoff%20frequency.%20How%20many%20decibels%20does%20each%20order%20attenuate%20there%3F%20Does%20it%20match%20%24-6%24%20dB%20per%20octave%20per%20order%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20noise%20in%20Pezzack's%20data%20extends%20up%20to%20the%20Nyquist%20frequency%2C%20about%2025%20Hz.%20With%20a%205%20Hz%20cutoff%2C%20roughly%20how%20much%20would%20a%20second-order%20filter%20attenuate%20noise%20at%2020%20Hz%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20not%20always%20use%20a%20very%20high%20order%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%203.**%20For%20an%20analog%20second-order%20Butterworth%20filter%2C%20estimate%20the%20attenuation%20at%20twice%20and%20four%20times%20its%20cutoff.%20Are%20%24-6%24%20dB%20per%20octave%20per%20order%20exact%20at%20the%20cutoff%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%203%0A%20%20%20%20The%20magnitude%20is%20%241%2F%5Csqrt%7B1%2B(f%2Ff_c)%5E4%7D%24.%20At%20ratios%202%20and%204%20the%20gains%20are%20about%20%24-12.30%24%20and%20%24-24.10%24%20dB.%20The%20%24-12%24%20dB%2Foctave%20slope%20is%20a%20high-frequency%20asymptote%2C%20not%20an%20exact%20rule%20at%20every%20frequency.%20Higher%20order%20attenuates%20more%20strongly%20but%20changes%20phase%20and%20can%20increase%20ringing%3B%20digital%20frequencies%20also%20undergo%20warping.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Butterworth%20filter%20with%20zero-phase%20shift%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20phase%20introduced%20by%20the%20Butterworth%20filter%20can%20be%20cancelled%20in%20a%20digital%20implementation%20by%20filtering%20the%20data%20twice%2C%20once%20forward%20and%20once%20backwards.%20The%20lag%20introduced%20in%20the%20first%20pass%20is%20undone%20by%20the%20same%20lag%20in%20the%20opposite%20direction%20in%20the%20second%20pass.%20The%20result%20is%20a%20zero-phase%20shift%20(or%20zero-phase%20lag)%20filter.%20Note%20that%20it%20needs%20the%20whole%20recording%20to%20run%20backwards%20from%20its%20end%2C%20so%20it%20cannot%20be%20used%20in%20real%20time.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20There%20is%20a%20catch.%20Each%20pass%20attenuates%20the%20power%20at%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20by%20half%2C%20so%20two%20passes%20attenuate%20it%20by%20a%20quarter%2C%20and%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20of%20the%20combined%20filter%20is%20no%20longer%20the%20one%20we%20asked%20for.%20We%20have%20to%20correct%20the%20cutoff%20given%20to%20%60butter%60%20so%20that%2C%20after%20both%20passes%2C%20the%20attenuation%20is%20again%20by%20half.%20For%20a%20second-order%20Butterworth%20filter%20applied%20%24n%24%20times%2C%20the%20correction%20factor%20is%20(Winter%2C%202009)%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20C%20%3D%20%5Csqrt%5B4%5D%7B2%5E%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7Bn%7D%7D%20-%201%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20two%20passes%2C%20%24n%3D2%24%2C%20%24C%3D%5Csqrt%5B4%5D%7B2%5E%7B%5Cfrac%7B1%7D%7B2%7D%7D%20-%201%7D%20%5Capprox%200.802%24%2C%20and%20the%20low-frequency%20approximation%20to%20the%20design%20cutoff%20is%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%20%20%20%20f_%7Bc%2C%5C%2Cdesign%7D%20%5Capprox%20%5Cfrac%7Bf_%7Bc%2C%5C%2Cdesired%7D%7D%7BC%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20For%20instance%2C%20this%20approximation%20suggests%2012.47%20Hz%20for%20a%20desired%2010%20Hz%20cutoff.%20A%20digital%20filter%20uses%20a%20bilinear%20transformation%2C%20so%20the%20exact%20correction%20must%20be%20made%20in%20the%20prewarped%20frequency%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%24f_%7Bc%2C%5C%2Cdesign%7D%3D%5Cfrac%7Bf_s%7D%7B%5Cpi%7D%5Carctan%5C!%5Cleft(%5Cfrac%7B%5Ctan(%5Cpi%20f_%7Bc%2C%5C%2Cdesired%7D%2Ff_s)%7D%7BC%7D%5Cright).%24%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20At%20%24f_s%3D100%24%20Hz%2C%20this%20gives%20about%2012.25%20Hz.%20The%20examples%20below%20use%20this%20exact%20correction.%20The%20effective%20cutoff%20is%20the%20frequency%20where%20the%20combined%20two-pass%20power%20gain%20is%20%241%2F2%24%2C%20or%20approximately%20%24-3.01%24%20dB.%20The%20combined%20response%20has%20fourth-order%20roll-off%20but%20is%20not%20an%20ordinary%20single-pass%20fourth-order%20Butterworth%20response.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20SciPy's%20function%20%60filtfilt%60%20does%20the%20forward%20and%20backward%20filtering.%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%20where%20the%20filtfilt%20curve%20will%20be%20relative%20to%20the%20raw%20data%20and%20to%20the%20single-pass%20filter.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(bw_t%2C%20bw_y%2C%20bw_y2%2C%20fs%2C%20np%2C%20plt%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20correct%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20for%20the%20two%20passes%20of%20the%20filter%0A%20%20%20%20C%20%3D%20(2**0.5%20-%201)**0.25%0A%20%20%20%20_b%2C%20_a%20%3D%20signal.butter(2%2C%20(2%20%2F%20np.pi)%20*%20np.arctan(np.tan(np.pi%20*%205%20%2F%20fs)%20%2F%20C)%2C%20btype%3D%22low%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_y3%20%3D%20signal.filtfilt(_b%2C%20_a%2C%20bw_y)%20%20%23%20zero-phase%20filtering%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_ax%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%201%2C%20figsize%3D(9%2C%204))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(bw_t%2C%20bw_y%2C%20%22r.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22raw%20data%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(bw_t%2C%20bw_y2%2C%20%22b.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22lfilter%20%40%205%20Hz%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(bw_t%2C%20_y3%2C%20%22g.-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22filtfilt%20%40%205%20Hz%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.legend(frameon%3DFalse)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_ylabel(%22Amplitude%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%20(C%2C)%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20filtfilt%20output%20sits%20right%20on%20the%20slow%20part%20of%20the%20raw%20data%2C%20with%20no%20delay%2C%20with%20much%20smaller%20edge%20transients%20than%20this%20zero-initialized%20single%20pass.%20Padding%20reduces%20boundary%20artifacts%3B%20it%20does%20not%20guarantee%20their%20absence.%20Let's%20also%20check%20the%20correction%3A%20at%205%20Hz%2C%20one%20pass%20of%20the%20corrected%20filter%20should%20attenuate%20by%20about%201.5%20dB%2C%20so%20that%20two%20passes%20attenuate%20by%203%20dB.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(C%2C%20fs%2C%20np%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_h%20%3D%20signal.freqz(*signal.butter(2%2C%20(2%20%2F%20np.pi)%20*%20np.arctan(np.tan(np.pi%20*%205%20%2F%20fs)%20%2F%20C))%2C%20worN%3D%5B5%5D%2C%20fs%3Dfs)%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_h0%20%3D%20signal.freqz(*signal.butter(2%2C%205%20%2F%20(fs%20%2F%202))%2C%20worN%3D%5B5%5D%2C%20fs%3Dfs)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22Gain%20at%205%20Hz%2C%20corrected%20cutoff%3A%20%20%20one%20pass%20%7B20%20*%20np.log10(abs(_h%5B0%5D))%3A.2f%7D%20dB%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22two%20passes%20%7B40%20*%20np.log10(abs(_h%5B0%5D))%3A.2f%7D%20dB%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20print(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22Gain%20at%205%20Hz%2C%20uncorrected%20cutoff%3A%20one%20pass%20%7B20%20*%20np.log10(abs(_h0%5B0%5D))%3A.2f%7D%20dB%2C%20%22%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20f%22two%20passes%20%7B40%20*%20np.log10(abs(_h0%5B0%5D))%3A.2f%7D%20dB%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%204.**%20A%20second-order%20Butterworth%20filter%20is%20applied%20forward%20and%20backward%20without%20correction.%20What%20is%20the%20combined%20gain%20at%20the%20single-pass%20cutoff%3F%20How%20can%20you%20check%20a%20corrected%20design%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%204%0A%20%20%20%20Each%20pass%20has%20amplitude%20%241%2F%5Csqrt2%24%2C%20so%20the%20combined%20amplitude%20is%20%241%2F2%24%20and%20the%20power%20is%20%241%2F4%24%3A%20%2420%5Clog_%7B10%7D(1%2F2)%3D-6.0206%24%20dB.%20Evaluate%20%60freqz%60%20at%20the%20desired%20frequency%3B%20for%20two%20passes%20require%20%60abs(h)**4%20%3D%200.5%60%2C%20or%20%6040*np.log10(abs(h))%20%3D%20-3.0103%60.%20The%20prewarped%20correction%20above%20satisfies%20this%20condition.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20Without%20the%20correction%2C%20filtering%20twice%20at%20a%20nominal%205%20Hz%20attenuates%205%20Hz%20by%206%20dB%3A%20the%20real%20cutoff%20would%20be%20lower%20than%20the%20one%20you%20report%20in%20your%20methods%20section.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Critically%20damped%20digital%20filter%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20problem%20with%20the%20low-pass%20Butterworth%20filter%20is%20that%20it%20tends%20to%20overshoot%20or%20undershoot%20data%20with%20rapid%20changes%20(see%2C%20for%20example%2C%20Winter%20(2009)%2C%20Robertson%20et%20al.%20(2013)%2C%20and%20Robertson%20and%20Dowling%20(2003)).%20The%20Butterworth%20filter%20behaves%20as%20an%20underdamped%20second-order%20system%3B%20the%20analog%20critically%20damped%20response%20avoids%20that%20overshoot.%20Its%20digital%20approximation%20must%20still%20be%20checked%2C%20especially%20close%20to%20Nyquist.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20function%20%60critic_damp%60%20below%20calculates%20the%20coefficients%20(the%20%24b%24's%20and%20%24a%24's)%20of%20an%20IIR%20critically%20damped%20digital%20filter%2C%20and%20corrects%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20for%20the%20number%20of%20passes%20of%20the%20filter.%20The%20calculation%20is%20very%20similar%20to%20that%20of%20the%20Butterworth%20filter%2C%20so%20the%20function%20can%20also%20calculate%20the%20Butterworth%20coefficients%20if%20asked%20to%3B%20only%20the%20damping%20term%20and%20the%20correction%20factor%20differ.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20critic_damp(fcut%2C%20freq%2C%20npass%3D2%2C%20fcorr%3DTrue%2C%20filt%3D%22critic%22)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Coefficients%20of%20a%20critically%20damped%20or%20Butterworth%20digital%20low-pass%20filter.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20A%20problem%20with%20a%20low-pass%20Butterworth%20filter%20is%20that%20it%20tends%20to%20overshoot%0A%20%20%20%20or%20undershoot%20data%20with%20rapid%20changes%20(see%20for%20example%2C%20Winter%20(2009)%2C%0A%20%20%20%20Robertson%20et%20al.%20(2013)%2C%20and%20Robertson%20%26%20Dowling%20(2003)).%0A%20%20%20%20The%20analog%20critically%20damped%20response%20avoids%20step%20overshoot.%20Check%20the%0A%20%20%20%20actual%20digital%20response%2C%20particularly%20for%20cutoffs%20near%20Nyquist.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Parameters%0A%20%20%20%20----------%0A%20%20%20%20fcut%20%3A%20number%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20desired%20cutoff%20frequency%20for%20the%20low-pass%20digital%20filter%20(Hz).%0A%20%20%20%20freq%20%3A%20number%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20sampling%20frequency%20(Hz).%0A%20%20%20%20npass%20%3A%20number%2C%20optional%20(default%20%3D%202)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20number%20of%20passes%20the%20filter%20will%20be%20applied.%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20choose%202%20for%20two%20passes%20of%20the%20second-order%20section%20(fourth-order%20roll-off).%0A%20%20%20%20fcorr%20%3A%20bool%2C%20optional%20(default%20%3D%20True)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20correct%20(True)%20or%20not%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20for%20the%20number%20of%20passes.%0A%20%20%20%20filt%20%3A%20string%20('critic'%2C%20'butter')%2C%20optional%20(default%20%3D%20'critic')%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20'critic'%20to%20calculate%20coefficients%20for%20a%20critically%20damped%20filter%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20'butter'%20to%20calculate%20coefficients%20for%20a%20Butterworth%20filter.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Returns%0A%20%20%20%20-------%0A%20%20%20%20b%20%3A%201D%20array%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20b%20coefficients%20for%20the%20filter%0A%20%20%20%20a%20%3A%201D%20array%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20a%20coefficients%20for%20the%20filter%0A%20%20%20%20fc%20%3A%20number%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20digital%20design-frequency%20parameter%20after%20exact%20prewarped%20correction%0A%0A%20%20%20%20References%0A%20%20%20%20----------%0A%20%20%20%20Robertson%20DG%2C%20Dowling%20JJ%20(2003)%20Design%20and%20responses%20of%20Butterworth%20and%0A%20%20%20%20critically%20damped%20digital%20filters.%20J%20Electromyogr%20Kinesiol%2013%2C%20569-573.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20filt%20%3D%20filt.lower()%0A%20%20%20%20if%20filt%20not%20in%20(%22critic%22%2C%20%22butter%22)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20raise%20ValueError(f%22Invalid%20option%20for%20parameter%20filt%3A%20%7Bfilt!r%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20if%20not%20np.isfinite(freq)%20or%20freq%20%3C%3D%200%20or%20not%200%20%3C%20fcut%20%3C%20freq%20%2F%202%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20raise%20ValueError(%22Require%20a%20positive%20sampling%20rate%20and%200%20%3C%20fcut%20%3C%20freq%2F2.%22)%0A%20%20%20%20if%20not%20np.isfinite(npass)%20or%20npass%20%3C%201%20or%20int(npass)%20!%3D%20npass%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20raise%20ValueError(%22npass%20must%20be%20a%20positive%20integer.%22)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Correct%20the%20prewarped%20frequency%2C%20not%20its%20digital%20frequency%20in%20hertz.%0A%20%20%20%20corr%20%3D%201.0%0A%20%20%20%20if%20fcorr%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20if%20filt%20%3D%3D%20%22critic%22%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20corr%20%3D%201%20%2F%20np.sqrt(2%20**%20(1%20%2F%20(2%20*%20npass))%20-%201)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20else%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20corr%20%3D%201%20%2F%20(2%20**%20(1%20%2F%20npass)%20-%201)%20**%200.25%0A%20%20%20%20wc%20%3D%20np.tan(np.pi%20*%20fcut%20%2F%20freq)%20*%20corr%0A%20%20%20%20fc%20%3D%20freq%20%2F%20np.pi%20*%20np.arctan(wc)%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20low-pass%20coefficients%0A%20%20%20%20k1%20%3D%20np.sqrt(2)%20*%20wc%20if%20filt%20%3D%3D%20%22butter%22% %20be%20computed%20after%20a%20moving%20average%20instead%20of%20before%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%206%0A%20%20%20%20The%20convolution%20version%20averages%20squared%20samples%20over%20a%20rectangle%20of%20length%20%242m%2B1%24.%20The%20forward%E2%80%93backward%20version%20applies%20an%20%24m%24-sample%20rectangle%20twice%2C%20giving%20a%20triangular%20interior%20weighting%20of%20length%20%242m-1%24%2C%20with%20different%20edge%20handling.%20These%20are%20different%20estimators.%20Averaging%20a%20signed%20EMG%20first%20cancels%20positive%20and%20negative%20values%3B%20square%20first%2C%20average%2C%20then%20take%20the%20square%20root%20to%20measure%20amplitude.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20Moving-median%20filter%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20moving-median%20filter%20is%20similar%20in%20concept%20to%20the%20other%20moving%20filters%20but%20uses%20the%20median%20instead%20of%20the%20mean.%20Because%20the%20median%20ignores%20the%20extreme%20values%20in%20the%20window%2C%20it%20preserves%20abrupt%20changes%20better%20than%20the%20moving%20average%2C%20and%20it%20removes%20isolated%20spikes%20almost%20completely.%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20predict%20how%20each%20filter%20will%20treat%20the%20two%20jumps.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(np%2C%20plt%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20_rng%20%3D%20np.random.default_rng(seed%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_x%20%3D%20_rng.standard_normal(300)%20%2F%2010%0A%20%20%20%20_x%5B100%3A200%5D%20%2B%3D%201%0A%20%20%20%20_window%20%3D%2011%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_y%20%3D%20np.convolve(_x%2C%20np.ones(_window)%20%2F%20_window%2C%20%22same%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_y2%20%3D%20signal.medfilt(_x%2C%20_window)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_ax%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%201%2C%20figsize%3D(10%2C%204))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_x%2C%20%22b-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D1%2C%20label%3D%22raw%20data%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_y%2C%20%22r-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22moving%20average%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(_y2%2C%20%22g-%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22moving%20median%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.legend(frameon%3DFalse%2C%20loc%3D%22upper%20right%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_xlabel(%22Sample%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_ylabel(%22Amplitude%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20moving%20median%20keeps%20the%20jumps%20nearly%20vertical%2C%20where%20the%20moving%20average%20turns%20them%20into%20ramps.%20Both%20filters%20also%20show%20what%20happens%20at%20the%20ends%20of%20the%20data%3A%20%60np.convolve%60%20with%20%60'same'%60%20and%20%60medfilt%60%20pad%20the%20data%20with%20zeros%20beyond%20its%20edges%2C%20which%20here%2C%20where%20the%20signal%20is%20near%20zero%2C%20does%20little%20harm.%20Every%20filter%20has%20to%20make%20some%20assumption%20about%20the%20data%20it%20does%20not%20have%2C%20and%20the%20edges%20are%20where%20that%20shows.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%23%20More%20moving%20filters%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20library%20%5Bpandas%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fpandas.pydata.org%2F)%20has%20many%20types%20of%20%5Bmoving%20(rolling)%20window%20functions%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fpandas.pydata.org%2Fdocs%2Fuser_guide%2Fwindow.html)%3A%20mean%2C%20median%2C%20standard%20deviation%2C%20quantiles%2C%20weighted%20windows%20and%20others%2C%20as%20in%20%60pd.Series(x).rolling(11%2C%20center%3DTrue).mean()%60.%20They%20mark%20the%20edges%2C%20where%20the%20window%20is%20incomplete%2C%20with%20%60NaN%60%20instead%20of%20padding%20the%20data.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Filtering%20before%20differentiating%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Back%20to%20the%20fun %2C%20label%3D%22raw%20data%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%200%5D.plot(bw_t%2C%20_yf%2C%20%22b%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22filtered%20%40%205%20Hz%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%200%5D.set_ylabel(%22f%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%200%5D.legend(frameon%3DFalse)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%201%5D.set_title(%22Frequency%20domain%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%201%5D.plot(*_amplitude_spectrum(bw_y)%2C%20%22r%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22raw%20data%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%201%5D.plot(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20*_amplitude_spectrum(_yf)%2C%20%22b--%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2%2C%20label%3D%22filtered%20%40%205%20Hz%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%201%5D.set_ylabel(%22Amplitude%20of%20f%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B0%2C%201%5D.legend(frameon%3DFalse)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%200%5D.plot(bw_t%5B1%3A-1%5D%2C%20_ydd%2C%20%22r%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%200%5D.plot(bw_t%5B1%3A-1%5D%2C%20_yfdd%2C%20%22b%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%200%5D.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%200%5D.set_ylabel(%22f%20''%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%201%5D.plot(*_amplitude_spectrum(_ydd)%2C%20%22r%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%201%5D.plot(*_amplitude_spectrum(_yfdd)%2C%20%22b--%22%2C%20linewidth%3D2)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%201%5D.set_xlabel(%22Frequency%20%5BHz%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_axs%5B1%2C%201%5D.set_ylabel(%22Amplitude%20of%20f%20''%22)%0A%20%20%20%20plt.tight_layout()%0A%20%20%20%20plt.show()%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%207.**%20Compare%20lowering%20the%20cutoff%20to%203%20Hz%20with%20applying%20the%205%20Hz%20forward%E2%80%93backward%20filter%20twice.%20Which%20retains%20more%20of%20a%201%20Hz%20component%20while%20suppressing%20the%2010%20Hz%20interference%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%20details%20%7C%20Solution%20to%20Exercise%207%0A%20%20%20%20For%20the%20100%20Hz%20example%2C%20use%20the%20exact%20response%20to%20compare%3A%20the%20corrected%20two-pass%203%20Hz%20filter%20retains%20about%2099.5%25%20of%20the%201%20Hz%20amplitude%20and%20about%201.7%25%20of%20the%2010%20Hz%20amplitude.%20Applying%20the%20corrected%205%20Hz%20two-pass%20filter%20twice%20retains%20about%2099.9%25%20of%201%20Hz%20and%20about%201.4%25%20of%2010%20Hz.%20The%20latter%20keeps%20the%20slow%20component%20better%20here%2C%20but%20has%20higher%20total%20order%20and%20different%20boundary%2Fringing%20behavior.%20Neither%20choice%20is%20universally%20better.%0A%20%20%20%20%2F%2F%2F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20In%20the%20raw%20data%20the%2010%20Hz%20peak%20is%20a%20tenth%20of%20the%201%20Hz%20peak%3B%20in%20the%20raw%20second%20derivative%20it%20is%20about%20nine%20times%20*larger*%2C%20close%20to%20the%20factor%20of%2010%20in%20amplitude%20computed%20by%20hand%20(a%20little%20less%2C%20because%20a%20finite%20difference%20underestimates%20the%20derivative%20of%20a%20fast%20oscillation).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20After%20filtering%2C%20the%2010%20Hz%20peak%20of%20%24f%24%20has%20almost%20disappeared%3A%20it%20is%20about%201%25%20of%20the%20signal.%20And%20yet%20in%20the%20second%20derivative%20of%20the%20filtered%20data%20it%20is%20back%2C%20about%20as%20large%20as%20the%20signal%20itself.%20Nothing%20went%20wrong.%20Two%20passes%20of%20a%20second-order%20filter%20at%205%20Hz%20reduce%20the%20amplitude%20at%2010%20Hz%20only%20about%20eight%20times%2C%20and%20the%20second%20derivative%20multiplies%20it%20by%20100%20again.%20**A%20filter%20that%20looks%20perfect%20on%20the%20data%20can%20be%20far%20too%20weak%20for%20their%20derivatives**%3B%20how%20much%20attenuation%20you%20need%20depends%20on%20how%20many%20times%20you%20will%20differentiate.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%202.**%20Change%20the%20cutoff%20frequency%20in%20the%20cell%20above%20to%203%20Hz%2C%20then%20go%20back%20to%205%20Hz%20and%20filter%20twice%20with%20%60filtfilt%60%20(four%20passes%20in%20all).%20Which%20works%20better%20for%20%24f''%24%3F%20What%20does%20each%20choice%20cost%20the%201%20Hz%20signal%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Pezzack's%20benchmark%20data%2C%20again%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Now%20we%20can%20attack%20the%20problem%20from%20the%20beginning%20of%20the%20notebook.%20The%20noise%20in%20Pezzack's%20angle%20comes%20from%20small%20random%20errors%20in%20the%20digitization%20of%20each%20frame%2C%20so%20it%20is%20spread%20up%20to%20the%20Nyquist%20frequency%2C%20above%20the%20frequency%20content%20of%20the%20movement.%20Let's%20try%20three%20different%20methods%20to%20attenuate%20it%3A%20a%20%5BButterworth%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FButterworth_filter)%20filter%2C%20a%20%5BSavitzky-Golay%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FSavitzky%25E2%2580%2593Golay_filter)%20filter%2C%20and%20a%20smoothing%20%5Bspline%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FSpline_function).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20Savitzky-Golay%20filter%20and%20the%20spline%20both%20fit%20polynomials%20to%20the%20data%2C%20and%20both%20can%20differentiate%20the%20fitted%20polynomials%20to%20get%20the%20derivatives%20directly%2C%20instead%20of%20differentiating%20the%20data%20numerically.%20Their%20signatures%20in%20SciPy%20are%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60python%0A%20%20%20%20savgol_filter(x%2C%20window_length%2C%20polyorder%2C%20deriv%3D0%2C%20delta%3D1.0%2C%20axis%3D-1%2C%20mode%3D'interp'%2C%20cval%3D0.0)%0A%20%20%20%20splrep(x%2C%20y%2C%20w%3DNone%2C%20xb%3DNone%2C%20xe%3DNone%2C%20k%3D3%2C%20task%3D0%2C%20s%3DNone%2C%20t%3DNone%2C%20full_output%3D0%2C%20per%3D0%2C%20quiet%3D1)%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60%0A%0A%20%20%20%20and%20the%20spline%20derivatives%20are%20evaluated%20with%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60python%0A%20%20%20%20splev(x%2C%20tck%2C%20der%3D0%2C%20ext%3D0)%0A%20%20%20%20%60%60%60%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Both%20fits%20behave%20poorly%20at%20the%20ends%20of%20the%20data%2C%20where%20there%20are%20points%20on%20only%20one%20side.%20A%20common%20workaround%20is%20to%20pad%20the%20data%20before%20fitting%2C%20with%20an%20*odd%20extension*%3A%20the%20data%20reflected%20about%20their%20first%20and%20last%20values%2C%20which%20continues%20the%20trend%20of%20the%20data%20instead%20of%20flattening%20it.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.function%0Adef%20odd_extension(x%2C%20n)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22Extend%20%60x%60%20by%20%60n%60%20samples%20at%20each%20end%2C%20reflected%20about%20its%20end%20values.%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%0A%20%20%20%20x%20%3D%20np.asarray(x)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20np.concatenate((2%20*%20x%5B0%5D%20-%20x%5Bn%3A0%3A-1%5D%2C%20x%2C%202%20*%20x%5B-1%5D%20-%20x%5B-2%20%3A%20-n%20-%202%20%3A%20-1%5D))%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20We%20will%20compare%20the%20methods%20with%20the%20%5Broot-mean-square%20error%20(RMSE)%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FRoot-mean-square_deviation)%20of%20each%20estimated%20acceleration%20relative%20to%20the%20measured%20reference%2C%20using%20the%20same%20interior%20samples%20for%20every%20method.%20The%20plain%20double%20difference%20had%20an%20RMSE%20of%20about%2011%20rad%2Fs%C2%B2.%20**Before%20you%20run%20the%20next%20cell**%2C%20guess%20how%20much%20each%20method%20will%20reduce%20it%3A%20by%20half%2C%20by%20a%20factor%20of%20ten%2C%20more%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_(C%2C%20interpolate%2C%20np%2C%20plt%2C%20pz_aacc%2C%20pz_disp%2C%20pz_dt%2C%20pz_time%2C%20signal)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Butterworth%20filter%20at%209%20Hz%2C%20zero%20phase%0A%20%20%20%20_b%2C%20_a%20%3D%20signal.butter(2%2C%20(2%20%2F%20np.pi)%20*%20np.arctan(np.tan(np.pi%20*%209%20*%20pz_dt)%20%2F%20C))%0A%20%20%20%20_aacc_bw%20%3D%20np.diff(signal.filtfilt(_b%2C%20_a%2C%20pz_disp)%2C%202)%20%2F%20pz_dt**2%20%20%23%202%20samples%20shorter%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20pad%20the%20data%20at%20the%20extremities%20to%20reduce%20edge%20effects%0A%20%20%20%20_n%20%3D%2011%0A%20%20%20%20_disp_pad%20%3D%20odd_extension(pz_disp%2C%20_n)%0A%20%20%20%20_time_pad%20%3D%20odd_extension(pz_time%2C%20_n)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20Savitzky-Golay%20filter%0A%20%20%20%20_aacc_sg%20%3D%20signal.savgol_filter(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20_disp_pad%2C%20window_length%3D5%2C%20polyorder%3D3%2C%20deriv%3D2%2C%20delta%3Dpz_dt%0A%20%20%20%20)%5B_n%3A-_n%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%23%20quintic%20smoothing%20spline%0A%20%20%20%20_s%20%3D%200.15%20*%20np.var(_disp_pad)%20%2F%20np.size(_disp_pad)%0A%20%20%20%20_tck%20%3D%20interpolate.splrep(_time_pad%2C%20_disp_pad%2C%20k%3D5%2C%20s%3D_s)%0A%20%20%20%20_aacc_sp%20%3D%20interpolate.splev(_time_pad%2C%20_tck%2C%20der%3D2)%5B_n%3A-_n%5D%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_rmse_bw%20%3D%20np.sqrt(np.mean((_aacc_bw%20-%20pz_aacc%5B1%3A-1%5D)%20**%202))%0A%20%20%20%20_rmse_sg%20%3D%20np.sqrt(np.mean((_aacc_sg%5B1%3A-1%5D%20-%20pz_aacc%5B1%3A-1%5D)%20**%202))%0A%20%20%20%20_rmse_sp%20%3D%20np.sqrt(np.mean((_aacc_sp%5B1%3A-1%5D%20-%20pz_aacc%5B1%3A-1%5D)%20**%202))%0A%0A%20%20%20%20_%2C%20_ax%20%3D%20plt.subplots(1%2C%201%2C%20figsize%3D(11%2C%204.5))%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(pz_time%2C%20pz_aacc%2C%20%22g%22%2C%20linewidth%3D3%2C%20label%3D%22Accelerometer%20(reference)%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(pz_time%5B1%3A-1%5D%2C%20_aacc_bw%2C%20%22r%22%2C%20label%3Df%22Butterworth%209%20Hz%3A%20RMSE%20%3D%20%7B_rmse_bw%3A.2f%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(pz_time%2C%20_aacc_sg%2C%20%22b%22%2C%20label%3Df%22Savitzky-Golay%205%20points%3A%20RMSE%20%3D%20%7B_rmse_sg%3A.2f%7D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.plot(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20pz_time%2C%20_aacc_sp%2C%20%22m%22%2C%20label%3Df%22Quintic%20spline%2C%20s%20%3D%20%7B_s%3A.5f%7D%3A%20RMSE%20%3D%20%7B_rmse_sp%3A.2f%7D%22%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_xlabel(%22Time%20%5Bs%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%20_ax.set_ylabel(%22Angular%20acceleration%20%5Brad%2Fs%24%5E2%24%5D%22)%0A%20%20%20%
